# Milestone M1: one-arm bench kit (generated by `python -m rnd.m1_kit`)

**Buy now: $1,218 + 15% contingency = $1,401.** Hold A (GIM8108-8 at pitch + elbow): **+$57** vs the GIM6010 default (up to +$285 at the dearest listing). Hold B (inline GIM8108-36 roll): **+$108** vs the belt roll (up to +$214). All with contingency.

| Scenario (with contingency) | M1 kit |
|---|---|
| Buy now only (yaw, wrist and everything else; pitch / roll / elbow motors not yet) | $1,401 |
| Both holds answered no (today's params: 4 × GIM6010-8, belt roll) | $1,761 |
| Hold A yes, hold B no (D20) | $1,818 |
| Both yes (D20 + inline roll) | $1,927 |

12 of the 33 buy-now lines are priced from retailer snapshots, 21 are ESTIMATE. Everything except the bench supply and the catch is reused in the full robot.

**Zero-regret shortcut:** if you want all four GIM joints turning on day 1 before the seller answers, buy the GIM6010-8s of both holds' *no* lists now (+3 × $90): the full robot needs at least 7 of them anyway (4 wheels, lift, 2 yaws), so a GIM6010 that a hold later replaces moves to the base. The GIM8108s are the only parts that wait.

**What M1 proves on real hardware:** joint strength, belts and the D13 v3 stages with the Oldham drive; the bolted cartridges (flange screws, centring lip, Oldham lash); the balancer (A9); hand accuracy with the joint encoders (≤ 1 mm target) and the compliance chain (rnd/stiffness.py); the fin-ray grasp and the D16 wrist spindle; motor and can temperatures (A6), CAN timing (SW1, A14), e-stop and watchdog time (SW2) with sw/bringup.py.

## 4. Questions for the seller (send as one message, before paying for any GIM)

1. **GIM8108-8, 24 V:** we run a 24 V bus (6S Li-ion, 25.2 V full; our regen clamp holds it ≤ 26.5 V, absolute max 28 V). Which driver version of the GIM8108-8 (SDC104, GDZ468, GDS68?) do you ship, and is it specified for 24 V? Please give rated torque, rated speed, no-load speed and continuous current at 24 V (listings quote 48 V). Price and lead time for 2 now (4 later).
2. **GIM8108-8 drawing:** installation drawing with frame diameter and height, output-flange bolt pattern (hole count, PCD, thread, depth) and housing / rear mounting pattern, and the connector position.
3. **GIM8108-36 (SDC303, 24 V) drawing:** frame diameter and overall height with the driver (one listing says Ø96 × 57 mm), output-flange pattern (hole count, PCD, thread, depth, centring spigot Ø), rear / housing mounting pattern, connector position.
4. **GIM8108-36 output bearing:** bearing type and allowable radial load at the output flange: we need **≈ 280 N radial** continuous, with a second support bearing 68 mm behind the flange; also the allowable axial load and tilting moment (one listing gives 1000 N radial / 250 N axial: please confirm and say where it is measured). Price with the SDC303 driver and lead time.
5. **CAN protocol manual** for the SDC104 (GIM6010-8), SDC303 (GIM8108-36) and the GIM8108-8's driver: frame formats; an MIT / impedance mode (position, velocity, kp, kd, torque feed-forward) and its float ranges; how to set the node ID and the feedback ID; 1 Mbit/s support; the CAN-timeout (heartbeat) setting; a torque / current-limit parameter saved to flash; encoder zero; status and error codes; under/over-voltage behaviour. Is it the same protocol on all three drivers?
6. **GIM6010-8:** confirm the unit is the 24 V **SDC104** version (not a 48 V listing), with its installation drawing.

Ask Damiao (or the DM-J4310 reseller) separately: the V1.1 output bearing's allowable radial load and moment.

## What changed since the loop-40 list

- **D24 bolted cartridges:** the KX socket hardware is gone from the arm (30 dowels, 15 G25 balls, 30 coil springs, retainers: −$34) and so are the cartridge torque pins (−$6; the flange screws take the torque). In: Oldham couplings (one per GIM stage) + acetal rod for spare discs, M4 / M3 heat-set inserts, the countersunk flange screws. The 4 rigid flange couplings of the D13 v2 stage go (−$20): the Oldham clamp hub sits on the shaft instead.
- **D19 one-piece shafts:** pitch, roll, yaw and elbow big pulleys are printed on their Ø40 tubes; no split pulleys, keys or double-D parts to buy. The seat caps are printed and bolted (2 × M4 / M3 into inserts).
- **A5 v2** (verified in this list): energy-rated regen clamp, DC contactor with aux contact, switched pre-charge, watchdog, bench catch.
- **Bring-up tool (sw/bringup.py):** 2 × $19 candleLight adapters (can0 / can1 per can_map.yaml, onboard 120 Ω for the adapter end) in place of 2 × $35; the GPIO / reset-button / opto parts for `--estop gpiod`; an adjustable current-limited supply for the 1 A first power-up.
- **Split into three lists:** the pitch, elbow and roll motors and the parts that depend on them move into the two holds.

## Check before paying / on arrival

- GIM6010-8: the **24 V SDC104** version; DM-J4310-2EC: **V1.1** (ask for the output bearing's radial / moment rating: the wrist pitch sees ≈ 0.9 N·m bending, more with the basket hook); STS3215: the **12 V C018**.
- Aluminium HTD 5M pulleys: 15 mm belt, **12 mm bore** (many default to 8 mm), two set screws.
- Oldham couplings: **12 mm clamp-style** hub, OD ≤ Ø42 (the cartridge nose bore is Ø43); measure the disc (thickness, slot width and depth) and set `OLDHAM` in rnd/parts/cartridge_m.py before printing the tongue adapters.
- Heat-set inserts: the short M4 (5.7 mm) the flange calls for; the long 8.1 mm ones don't fit the 6 mm flange.
- Belts: closed HTD **5M**, 15 mm wide (± 5 mm is taken up by the eccentric bushings).

**Order of work:** the coupons ([COUPONS.md](COUPONS.md); C1, the D15 socket, now needs re-scoping to the bolted flange + Oldham tongue) can run once the P2S arrives; nothing bought here depends on a coupon result. Readiness and the day-1 plan: [M1_READINESS.md](M1_READINESS.md). Buying is the owner's decision.
